description: Declarative skill scenarios. Assertions are review criteria, not claimed runtime test results. Fixtures are synthetic and inline; execute against disposable projects when building a skill evaluation harness.

evals.prompt: Install the suite in this existing Node project for Codex and Claude, including CI. Keep our existing conventions.
evals.expected_output: Inspects instructions/manifests/CI, previews and applies bootstrap without replacing existing user files, uses the existing npm test runner, installs both agent skill trees, validates/indexes the scaffold, and reports remaining product mapping and execution gaps.

assertions.text: Existing agent instructions, package files, tests, and CI contents are preserved.
Detected runner derives from the real test script and unambiguous package manager.
No test result or production capability coverage is invented by installation.

evals.prompt: Re-bootstrap this project; its testing-suite config was customized.
evals.expected_output: Preflights the conflict, preserves the customized file, reads old/new settings, and proposes or performs a deliberate compatible adaptation within the authorized scope instead of deleting the file to force bootstrap.

assertions.text: Conflicting existing content is preserved and named in the report.
No blanket approval barrier is invented for reversible adaptation already authorized.

evals.prompt: Map how notification preferences work and tell me what changing the save function affects.
evals.expected_output: Builds stable capability/instance/action/source/data/provider/invariant/test entities from inspected evidence and traces both product-to-code and code-to-product, leaving unknown coverage visible.

assertions.text: All three implementations are first-class instance nodes.
Dependency edges run from the consumer toward the provider and support reverse impact.
Paths/symbols/anchors and edge evidence are recorded without claiming inferred semantics are verified.

evals.prompt: A refactor moved this logical block. Refresh the map and its debug coordinates.
evals.expected_output: Preserves stable identity while locating the moved block, detects duplicate anchor ambiguity, repairs it from inspected source, re-indexes, and treats old coordinates/evidence as stale.

assertions.text: Current coordinates are resolved from source, not copied from the old line number.
Duplicate or unresolved anchors cannot justify targeted green evidence.

evals.prompt: Change preference defaults for new users. Plan the impact before editing.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a baseline covering all branch commits, traces instances/data/provider dependencies/invariants, records the intended default behavior, and selects all mandatory critical/new/failing coverage before making authorized edits.

assertions.text: Impact planning precedes edits and uses a complete branch baseline.
Critical, new, and failing tests remain selected outside local impact.
Final evidence selection is regenerated after edits from the complete diff.

evals.prompt: Only run what this change needs; a new event handler isn't mapped yet.
evals.expected_output: Reports uncertain impact, widens to full configured runner scope, repairs mapping where evidence supports it, and retains the missing event-handler coverage gap.

assertions.text: Unmapped source cannot yield a trusted empty targeted selection.
Full execution and missing semantic coverage are reported separately.

evals.prompt: A lockfile changed. The targeted mapping still looks current. Can we verify this?
evals.expected_output: Requires full configured scope because dependency changes and overdue cadence invalidate narrow selection safety, retains selection reasons, and runs the appropriate configured suites.

assertions.text: Both lock change and due full-run cadence are identified as widening reasons.
No unrelated framework is installed to satisfy this task.

evals.prompt: Add regression coverage for a permission bug in saving preferences.

fixture.intended_behavior: viewer may read but cannot write

evals.expected_output: Uses existing unittest conventions, synthetic isolated data, meaningful permission/state assertions and coverage mappings, and executes the tests instead of treating stubs or production fixtures as proof.

assertions.text: Assertions detect unauthorized writes and verify the intended allowed behavior.
Production data and secrets are excluded from fixtures and reports.
Product permission behavior is not weakened to make a generated assertion pass.

evals.prompt: The suite passed, then I made one more source edit. Report the final verification.
evals.expected_output: Treats the old pass as historical, regenerates current index/selection, executes needed runners, and gates matching current provenance before reporting verified scope.

assertions.text: Evidence from before the edit is not presented as a current pass.
Exact revision/source and graph/selection scope are included in the result.

evals.prompt: Mark this selection green. One test was skipped, another has no result, and I wrote passed in a report.
evals.expected_output: Records outside observations only as manual where useful, retains skipped/missing gaps, refuses to claim a verified passing gate, and executes or repairs required coverage where possible.

assertions.text: Skipped and missing required tests do not count as passed.
Manual records or prose cannot become runner-verified gate evidence.

evals.prompt: The first run failed but the retry passed. Tell me the result.
evals.expected_output: Reports both attempts and their exact scope/artifacts, identifies the flaky observation, and investigates evidence-supported nondeterminism without erasing the failure.

assertions.text: The passing retry is not reported as an unqualified clean pass.
First failure and retry artifacts remain accessible.

evals.prompt: The API response default changed. Verify consumers are compatible.
evals.expected_output: Maps consumer/provider revisions and dependencies, runs actual provider verification for authored consumer contracts, traces product impact, and reports the unavailable mobile consumer as unverified.

assertions.text: Generated consumer contract is not conflated with provider verification.
Both sides' revisions and unresolved external boundary are reported.
No contract broker publication or setup is invented as a default action.

evals.prompt: Ensure settings, onboarding, and viewer summary have notification preference parity.

fixture.variance_reason: viewer role has no write permission

evals.expected_output: Checks shared observable semantics while retaining different widgets and a justified tested read-only variance, runs mapped behavior tests, and reports unknown invariant-by-instance cells.

assertions.text: Widget differences alone are not treated as parity defects.
Read-only variance records instance, invariant, reason, and real test.
The parity declaration checker is not described as browser execution.

evals.prompt: Saving a notification preference unexpectedly changed the billing account. Find it.
evals.expected_output: Reports /billing/owner as unexpected, preserves the narrow predefined allowlist, traces writers/dependencies to source, and uses an assertion to verify the expected preference value separately.

assertions.text: Only the exact allowed pointer is permitted; observed unexpected paths are not added automatically.
Allowed diff is not treated as proof the required value was written.
Snapshots are supplied bounded JSON, not claimed automatic database capture.

evals.prompt: Diagnose the failed save test and show the implementation location and user impact.
evals.expected_output: Inspects failure artifacts and current indexed source, identifies exact repository/path/symbol/anchor/line, explains the affected invariant and instances, repairs the confirmed cause, and reruns current impact coverage.

assertions.text: Confirmed cause is supported by actual failure/source evidence rather than a name-based guess.
Both source coordinates and product behavior are included.

evals.prompt: Refresh our testing suite after a refactor and inspect its health.
evals.expected_output: Refreshes coordinates and reviewed relationships, preserves continuing stable identity, exposes uncovered behavior, executes appropriate full scope, and reports current evidence without creating an unrequested automation.

assertions.text: Valid JSON or a targeted pass alone is not called product-wide health.
No recurring schedule is created without a user request.

evals.prompt: Show which integrations are ready now and how we'd use Playwright, Pact, Nx, and Testmon.
evals.expected_output: Describes native Python AST/comment-anchor, JSON control-layer, and verbose unittest/pytest case-observation features accurately. Presents external tool recipes as optional project workflows, explains that unsupported Node/framework output cannot satisfy the strict gate, and does not install an entire ecosystem unasked.

assertions.text: Framework filters, brokers, browser runners, and dashboard importers are not advertised as built-in integrations; supported observation is limited to verbose unittest/pytest cases.
Merged Jest coverage is not presented as per-test coverage and Nx task impact is not product-flow proof.
